subject: Temporary subprocessor access request — PulseLogs (EU logs)
messages:
From: Sophie Larkin <sophie.larkin@acme-retail.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: temporary subprocessor access for log review

Hi Aisha / Marissa,

Quick one from our side: our security team is completing a limited-scope audit of recent production incidents and has requested that PulseLogs (a third-party log-aggregation vendor) be granted temporary, read-only access to a subset of our logs stored in the EU region for the period Jun 1–Jun 10.

As part of the procurement checklist, we also need an explicit subprocessor roster that includes: the vendor name, data categories processed, location of processing, and the contractual DPA clause references (or an addendum). Can you confirm whether PulseLogs is already listed as a subprocessor in Redwood's DPA and, if not, how quickly Redwood can provide a one-off addendum or evidence of SCC/transfer basis for EU processing?

I've attached the section from our DPA that lists required evidence fields for subprocessors. Happy to hop on a short call if it helps — time is tight on our side.

Thanks,
Sophie Larkin
Head of IT Risk, Acme Retail
[Attachment: acme_subproc_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Larkin <sophie.larkin@acme-retail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 17:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: temporary subprocessor access for log review

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask.

Short answer: PulseLogs is not on our current EU subprocessor roster; they are listed for non-EU processing under a different contract. I have attached the DPA addendum PulseLogs provided last quarter (it covers SOC reports and encryption at rest) but does not reference EU transit explicitly.

Next steps I propose:
- I will loop in Legal and Security for a quick triage to confirm whether we can provide the requested temporary read-only access from our EU log-archive cluster.
- If Security approves, we can provide a limited access window and a short addendum (we typically use our standard subprocessor addendum template which references SCCs/UK Addendum as applicable).
- Please confirm the exact log buckets and retention window you need read access to (we can map to our internal prefixes).

Attaching: pulse_logs_dpa_addendum.pdf and a proposed access window spreadsheet (access_window_proposal.xlsx).

I'll follow up with Legal/Security now.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pulse_logs_dpa_addendum.pdf (PDF)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Sophie Larkin <sophie.larkin@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: temporary subprocessor access for log review

Aisha / Marissa — looping in Legal formally.

Thanks Sophie for the details and the attachment. High-level notes from Legal:
- We need a signed addendum or an explicit written acknowledgment from Acme accepting PulseLogs as a subprocessor for this limited window (our template is fastest).
- Please confirm whether the logs contain any PII categories beyond request/response metadata (IP addresses, user identifiers). If PII is present, we will require the following mitigations: encryption in transit, role-based access control for PulseLogs engineers, and an explicit delete/expiry action after Jun 20.
- On transfer basis: if PulseLogs will process in EU only and our contract references EU SCCs (or UK Addendum) we can rely on that; if they move data outside EU, we will need documented transfer mechanisms.

Rishi — can Security confirm the feasibility of instituting a read-only, time-bound IAM role scoped to the specific S3 prefixes and the log index? We would prefer RBAC + no-download policy if feasible.

Sophie — if you can reply with the specific prefixes or sample object keys and confirm PII status, we can expedite the addendum and access provisioning.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: access_window_proposal.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Larkin <sophie.larkin@acme-retail.com>, aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary subprocessor access for log review — plan and next steps

Sophie — quick update and plan so everyone has a single thread:

1) Action items for Acme: please confirm the exact log prefixes you want Pulselogs to read and whether the payloads include IPs or other identifiers (one-line reply is fine).
2) Legal: once we receive that confirmation, Laura will send our standard subprocessor addendum for signature (we can fast-track for a 48-hour turnaround).
3) Security: Rishi, please confirm whether RBAC + a no-download policy can be enforced and whether we can set the expiry to Jun 20 by policy.
4) Me (Sales): I will log this in HubSpot (company ACME-98765) and mark as a compliance milestone for the renewal. I will also create a short shared folder for the signed addendum and any evidence.

Sophie — if you prefer a 15-min call to accelerate, I have availability Tue 10:00–11:00 BST and Wed 09:00–10:00 BST. Otherwise a short reply here will suffice.

Thanks — aiming to have access window and signed addendum in place before Jun 1.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-98765]
